_readme: Hand-written replacements for the spreadsheet's auto-generated character guides.
The spreadsheet derives 'Main character' from the story title, which produces
nonsense like 'Main character: Bedtime'. Anything keyed by storyId here replaces
that block wholesale when build-manifest.js runs.
Beginner 4 is one continuous day in one child's life, so all five stories share
the same character description verbatim. Keep it identical when adding stories to
a set — identical wording is what holds the look together across separate
Target audience is Japanese ESL learners, so the recurring child is Japanese.
Change the description here if you'd rather vary it.
LEARNED FROM THE B4 PILOT (2026-08-07): character consistency held up well across four
separately-generated images — same face, hair, outfit throughout. Two things drifted, and
both need anchoring explicitly because the model will not infer them:
1. WORLD. Scene 3 came back as a British brick terrace with hydrangeas; scene 4 as a
Japanese suburb with cherry blossom. Always state the country and building style.
2. SEASON. Scene 4 mixed cherry blossom and autumn maples in one frame. Always state
the season and explicitly rule out the others.
Every guide below therefore carries an identical WORLD and SEASON line. Keep them verbatim
across a set — identical wording is what holds a set together across separate sessions.
_world: World: a modern Japanese suburban neighbourhood. The family home is a small contemporary Japanese house with a genkan entrance hall, sliding or panelled interior doors, and a low step where shoes are removed. No British or European brick terraces, no bay windows.
_season: Season: late spring — fresh green leaves, mild sunshine. No cherry blossom, no autumn colour, no snow. Keep the season identical in every image of the set.

- Season: late spring — fresh green leaves, mild sunshine. No cherry blossom, no autumn colour, no snow. Keep the season identical in every image of the set.
- Continuity note: this is story 1 of 5 following Mika through a single day. Keep her face, hair and outfit identical in every image of the set.

_b2_note: l1.2s1 and l1.2s2 rejected on first generation: the spreadsheet's auto-guide named the title object as 'Main character' with no child specified, so the model drew the apple/pen as an anthropomorphic character with a face and limbs, in one case eating itself. Fixed below by naming an actual child and explicitly forbidding personifying the object.
l1.2s1:
Character consistency guide:
- Main character: a cheerful child, about 6 years old, with light brown wavy hair to the shoulders worn loose, wearing a blue-and-white striped long-sleeve top and dark trousers.
- Supporting characters: none
- The apple: an ordinary, realistic red apple with a small stem and leaf. It is a plain piece of fruit, not a character — it must never have a face, eyes, arms, or legs, must never show any expression, and must never hold, eat, or use anything itself. The child holds and eats the apple; the apple never acts on its own.
- Setting: a cosy kitchen or dining table at home
- Continuity note: keep the child's face, hair and outfit identical in every image of this set.

- Main character: a cheerful child, about 6 years old, with light brown hair in a ponytail, wearing a striped top.
- Supporting characters: none
- The pen: an ordinary blue ballpoint pen. It is a plain writing tool, not a character — it must never have a face, eyes, arms, or legs, must never show any expression, and must never stand, sit, or write by itself. The child holds and writes with the pen; the pen never acts on its own.
- Setting: a bright, friendly classroom
- Continuity note: keep the child's face, hair and outfit identical in every image of this set.
